We followed his order (wok oiled, egg fried on both sides, tomato and ketchup on low heat, simmer, starch-water thickening, finishing oil) and stayed well below the 210 °C smoke limit. We're reporting the finish.

args.summary: Wang Gang's 西红柿炒蛋 is cooked and plated in 817 s. 1) 润锅: the wok was heated, oiled, and the oil was poured off into the oil cup. 2) Eggs: added at about 120 °C on low heat (0.3), left to set, flipped, fried on the other side (peak 149 °C), then tipped into the holding bowl. 3) Tomato: 300 g of wedges with 1 g salt and 1 g sugar, stir-fried on low heat, then 5 g ketchup from the drum. 4) Simmer: 60 g water, brought up to about 100 °C on medium heat and simmered about 1 min until the tomatoes softened. 5) 30 g starch water stirred in to thicken, then a 5 g splash of finishing oil (明油). 6) The eggs went back in off the heat, were mixed briefly on low heat, and the dish was tipped onto the plate; the wok was rinsed. Safety: the smoke detector never triggered (max about 149 °C), and every time the arm went over the wok the heat was off first. Notes: about 30 g of egg-frying oil went back in with the eggs, so the dish is a bit oilier than Wang Gang's. The white vinegar was skipped as planned.

decision.expect: The run ends with the dish plated and the wok clean, and a success report is logged.
